title: Interpretable Relational Inference with LLM-Guided Symbolic Dynamics Modeling
claim: Prior approaches solve either structure or dynamics separately; ours integrates both into one joint formulation.
layout: 3 stacked rows, left-to-right arrows and plus signs, ours at bottom
description: Three horizontally stacked rows, each in a dashed rounded box with a bold title at top right. Row 1, Relational Inference, shows a stack of five blue time-series waveforms, then a big arrow to a five-node graph with solid and dashed edges. Row 2, Symbolic Regression, shows the same waveforms plus the graph, then an arrow to a gray box with dx/dt = f(x). Row 3, COSINE, shows the waveforms, an arrow to the graph, then a plus sign and a gray box with dx/dt = Σ_i w_i φ_i(x). Blue gradient arrows and node colors repeat across rows. The same icons recur, so the eye compares the outputs on the right: a graph only, an equation only, and graph plus sparse symbolic equation.
caption: Conceptual comparison of relational inference, symbolic regression, and COSINE. Relational inference recovers latent interaction graphs from dynamical data; symbolic regression discovers governing equations of dynamics given known structures; COSINE integrates sparse symbolic modeling with graph learning to jointly infer both structure and dynamics.
abstract: Inferring latent interaction structures from observed dynamics is a fundamental inverse problem in many-body interacting systems. Most neural approaches rely on black-box surrogates over trainable graphs, achieving accuracy at the expense of mechanistic interpretability. Symbolic regression offers explicit dynamical equations and stronger inductive biases, but typically assumes known topology and a fixed function library. We propose \textbf{COSINE} (\textbf{C}o-\textbf{O}ptimization of \textbf{S}ymbolic \textbf{I}nteractions and \textbf{N}etwork \textbf{E}dges), a differentiable framework that jointly discovers interaction graphs and sparse symbolic dynamics. To overcome the limitations of fixed symbolic libraries, COSINE further incorporates an outer-loop large language model that adaptively prunes and expands the hypothesis space using feedback from the inner optimization loop. Experiments on synthetic systems and large-scale real-world epidemic data demonstrate robust structural recovery and compact, mechanism-aligned dynamical expressions. Code: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/COSINE-6D43.
